questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: This is one of the best places in the world to study arctic sciences. The nature also had a big influence on my decision.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Svalbard is a very special place and people who go here tend to fall in love with the place.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. You can find all the necessary information on unis' website (time schedule etc).

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I don't exactly remember, whether we got any specific assistance, but in general we are well taken care of.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Generally very satisfied. Only kinda tricky part was to figure out where my student housing was as google maps is not very good on Svalbard.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy. UNIS will send you a link to a housing portal through which you apply. All students live in the same buildings so the social life is very good.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Everyone lives off-campus. There is no on-campus options. 
It is difficult to find housing on Svalbard unless you're a student.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The buildings are new (from summer 2021) and I was one of fhe first students to live here.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There's is only a limited amount of courses and they come in course packages. So if you sign up for one of them you also must sign up for the other one. But it was very easy. When you apply to UNIS you apply to the courses, not the university itself. That means that if you're accepted you're automatically enrolled in your courses and don't need to do more.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is a student advisor at UNIS for each department (geology, biology, geophysics and technology).

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: None really. It's quite simple.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I'm very satisfied with the academic level at UNIS and the courses in general. It is very research based and you get to try both report writing with your own project, poster presentations etc (depending on which courses you attend of course). The fieldwork is also excellent and it's a good learning environment in general.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was a good level, not too hard. You can do more or less depending on how much time you are willing to invest, so it sort of depends on yourself how hard and detailed you want to make it (especially in your individual project).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: UNIS has a lot more field work. It is not the classical university experience with lectures and following exercises, but instead we have more integrated classes. In general there is a lot of practical work which I personally really like.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Marine geology
The quaternary and glacial geology of Svalbard

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer:
The tectonic and sedimentary history of Svalbard
Integrated Geological Methods: From Outcrop to Geomodel

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I particularly liked the marine geology course, because I'm really interested in marine science. We went on a week-long cruise to the north of Svalbard and had a lot of lab work, which was really cool. 
The other courses are also very good. It just depends on your interests!

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Food is ridiculously expensive! Be prepared to at least double your food budget compared to Denmark. 
Also, you'll probably find yourself buying a lot of outdoor equipment during your time up here :) especially if you're here in spring where you can rent or buy a snowscooter.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: FOOD!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university itself does not provide any non-academic opportunities, however Svalbard Turn is the local sport association and they provide volleyball, soccer, fitness clases, badminton, climbing etc for at very reasonable price.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: none by the host institution, but there's plenty of things going on around in the city. Seems like there is always some kind of festival going on.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Get out and go hiking! Go to the cabins for the students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: hike :) Look at the adorable reindeers :) there is surprisingly many things you can spend time on here. Most of them involve nature.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Everyone are exchange students and are keen on getting friends, so everyone are very open.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: You're living in the same building so just go to the kitchen and talk. Also, UNIS organises a friday gathering every week where all of UNIS staff and students are invited which is a good way to socialize across departments.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: like mentioned, there is not really a norwegian culture here because of all the exchange students.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Rest before you get here, because you won't have much time for it up here with all the hikes and things that are going on :) 
Save up money so you have enough to buy food and don't starve. 
Don't worry too much about making friends. It is no problem because people are so kind and open.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I can't think of any at the moment.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to go outside into the nature was so rewarding and amazing. The academics was also very rewarding and it made me realise that I want to pursue a degree within marine science.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Managing academics vs sparetime. Often you just want to go outside, but you need to work once in a while.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: enjoy! It's amazing.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
